1. What framework is being used (Next.js, React Router, etc.)
2. Files related to the home page and product page

Also defines top-level metadata (title: "Shop", description: "E-commerce product store") | ### Product page (`/product` route) | File | Purpose | |---|---| | `/vercel/sandbox/app/product/page.tsx` | The product page component. Fetches inventory data via `getInventory()` and renders product name, stock count, and price | | `/vercel/sandbox/lib/data.ts` | The data-fetching utility that `product/page.tsx` imports. Generates randomized inventory data after awaiting `connection()` from `next/server` | --- ## 3. Navigation Between Pages Navigation is handled by **Next.js ``** from `next/link`: - **`/vercel/sandbox/app/page.tsx` (line 8):** `View Product` — This is the sole navigation link. It uses Next.js's client-side router to navigate from `/` to `/product` without a full page reload. There are: - No `

Where Page Titles Are Rendered Page titles come from **Next.js Metadata API** in the root layout: - **`/vercel/sandbox/app/layout.tsx` (lines 3-6):** Exports a `metadata` object with `title: 'Shop'` and `description: 'E-commerce product store'`. Next.js renders this as `Shop` in the ``. There is **no per-page metadata override** in either `page.tsx`. So: - Home page title: "Shop" (from the root layout) - Product page title: "Shop" (also from the root layout — no product-specific `` is set) There are also visible `<h1>` headings in each page component (not the `<head>` title, but the on-screen heading): - `app/page.tsx` line 7: `<h1>Home</h1>` - `app/product/page.tsx` line 8: `<h1>Premium Widget</h1>` --- ## 5. Loading States and Data Fetching on the Product Page ### Data Fetching **`/vercel/sandbox/app/product/page.tsx`** is an **async Server Component** (notice `export default async function ProductPage()`). It: 1. Calls `const inventory = await getInventory()` at the top of the component. 2. `getInventory()` (in `/vercel/sandbox/lib/data.ts`) does two things: - **`await connection()`** — This is from `next/server`. `connection()` is an async function that resolves only after the incoming request's headers/body are fully available. This is a low-level Next.js API often used to opt into dynamic rendering (ensuring the page is server-rendered per request rather than statically cached). - Returns `{ count: <random 0-49>, price: <random 0-100.00> }` — randomized per request. Because the component is async and awaits `connection()`, this page opts into **dynamic rendering** (not static generation). The data is fetched on the server for every request. ### Loading States **There is no `loading.tsx` file anywhere in the `app/` directory.** Specifically: - No `/vercel/sandbox/app/loading.tsx` (root loading boundary) - No `/vercel/sandbox/app/product/loading.tsx` (product-specific loading boundary) This means: - While the product page's `getInventory()` is resolving, there is **no Suspense fallback/no loading UI** shown to the user. - The server will hold the response until the async work completes, then stream the full HTML to the client. - If you wanted a loading spinner or skeleton during server rendering, you would need to create `/vercel/sandbox/app/product/loading.tsx`. part.text:
The build succeeds and confirms the fix — `/product` is now `◐ (Partial Prerender)`, meaning it prerenders the static shell (including the `<h1>` title) immediately and streams the dynamic inventory data separately.

**What changed:**
- `app/product/page.tsx` — no longer async; renders the `<h1>` title immediately and wraps the async `<Inventory />` in `<Suspense>`
- `app/product/inventory.tsx` — new async component that fetches and renders inventory data

Previously, the `await getInventory()` at the top of the page blocked rendering of the entire page, including the title. Now the title renders instantly while inventory data streams in.
